name: James — Parkinson's disease, rural Montana
description: Distance is a real constraint; shows a levodopa timing near-miss with a concrete date and what telehealth or travel could open up.
firstMessage: My dad James is 67, has Parkinson's disease, and takes levodopa. We live outside Billings, Montana — is anything within reach for him?
answers: He was diagnosed about six years ago. His main symptoms are tremor and slowness, and lately the levodopa seems to wear off between doses.
He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100, two tablets three times a day. He hasn't had deep brain stimulation or any infusion therapies.
He's otherwise pretty healthy — type 2 diabetes controlled with metformin, and no memory problems.
He could manage a few hours by car. Flying is hard for him, so somewhere in Montana or a neighboring state would be best.
Yes, he'd be open to telehealth visits if a study allows them.
